B: Hiya! Oh, lovely, you're there. I'm Ceri.
A: Hi. Riya.
B: Where are you calling from, Riya?
A: London. Canada Water, south-east.
B: Oh, fancy. I'm in Pontypridd, South Wales. Rain and rugby, mostly. How was your puzzle bit at the start? I was rubbish, I think I panicked.
A: It was fine. I'm not sure the instructions were very clear, to be honest. Two of the questions seemed to contradict each other.
B: See, I thought that was just me being thick! Thank God. What do you do for work, then?
A: Operations manager for a grocery delivery company. I run planning for two warehouses and manage a team of seven.
B: Seven? Blimey. Do they behave?
A: Mostly. Some need more chasing than others.
B: Ha, I bet you're good at the chasing. I'm a student, mature student, occupational therapy at Cardiff. I'm forty-one before you ask.
A: I wasn't going to ask.
B: No, people usually do, you know, "oh, isn't that late to start?" Like there's a cut-off.
A: I don't think there is. My MSc had people in their forties. They were usually the ones who did the reading. What did you do before?
B: Hairdresser. Twenty years. So I can talk to anyone, which is basically the whole of OT anyway. Getting someone to tell you how they really manage the stairs when they say they're fine.
A: That's a useful skill. More useful than most of what I learned at business school, probably.
B: Aw, go on. What do you do outside work, then? You looked like a reader in your photo, all them books in a straight line.
A: I do read a lot. Mostly translated fiction. I'm halfway through a Korean novel at the moment.
B: Oh, I'm in a book club. Mostly I read thrillers, psychological ones, the twisty ones. The book club picks the literary stuff and I'm usually the one saying I didn't like it.
A: Which ones didn't you like?
B: Erm, the last one was all about a woman staring at the sea for three hundred pages. Nothing happened! Everyone else was going "oh, it's so subtle". I said, subtle? I wouldn't call it subtle, I'd call it boring.
A: That's fair, honestly. A lot of literary fiction is praised for being slow when it's just slow. I'd rather someone say that than pretend.
B: Thank you! See, I thought you'd be a sea-staring type.
A: Sometimes I am. It depends on whether the staring goes anywhere. Have you read any Han Kang? The Vegetarian?
B: No, is it a thriller?
A: Not exactly. It's quite disturbing, though. You might actually like it. It's short as well.
B: Short is good. I've got an essay due Friday I haven't started, so short is all I can cope with. I read on the train, when the train actually turns up, which is about half the time.
A: The Jubilee line's the same. Not late, just rammed. You end up reading with your elbow in someone's ear.
